title: Diaphragm Pump Preferred Over Centrifugal for Splash Water Gun — Self-Priming, High Pressure, Dry-Run Safe
context: Splash needs a micro pump for water gun payload (~15g, 12V, controllable). Pump type affects stream quality, reliability, and weight.
what_was_found: Agricultural spray drone engineering literature and competitor builds converge on the same conclusion: diaphragm pumps are superior for burst-fire water gun applications. Centrifugal pumps lack self-priming (fail if air enters line), lose pressure at low flow rates, and can't run dry. Diaphragm pumps are self-priming, handle air in line, run dry without damage, and deliver high-pressure pulses ideal for water gun bursts. Peristaltic pumps are precise but produce gentler flow — not ideal for maximum stream distance.

comparison.diaphragm: Self-priming ✅, dry-run safe ✅, high pressure ✅, pulsed flow ✅, ~15g — BEST for Splash
comparison.centrifugal: No self-priming ❌, fails with air ❌, low pressure at low flow ❌, continuous flow, ~12g — AVOID
comparison.peristaltic: Self-priming ✅, dry-run safe ✅, low pressure ❌, precise dosing, ~20g — only for precision, not range

source: Hour 7 Competitor Analysis — Agricultural drone literature + dave-ct/ai_object_plus_water pump teardown analysis
action: Source 12V micro diaphragm pump (e.g., HiLetgo 240L/H 4.2W or similar). Verify self-priming behavior and stream distance at 12V before integration.
